name: rapid-qoi
baseline: qoi crate 0.4 (a Rust QOI encoder/decoder; it is the 'qoi' column in the benchmark source bench/src/main.rs). Not libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp or libavif.
workload: In-memory QOI encode and decode of the RGBA pixels of the qoi_benchmark_suite PNG images (qoiformat.org), 5 runs per directory, grand total over the suite.
claimed_speedup: README grand total (ms, qoi vs rapid_qoi): Intel i9 decode 2.009 vs 1.404 (1.43x faster, derived from page data) and encode 2.706 vs 2.520 (1.07x, derived); Apple M1 decode 1.676 vs 1.100 (1.52x, derived) and encode 2.088 vs 1.836 (1.14x, derived). Throughput in Mpps (qoi vs rapid_qoi): i9 decode 231.01 vs 330.72, encode 171.52 vs 184.23; M1 decode 277.01 vs 421.99, encode 222.26 vs 252.77. README text: 'one of the most efficient implementations of QOI encoder and decoder'.
compiler_and_flags: Run with 'cargo run --release -p bench -- [iterations] [path]' (Rust release profile); rustc version and flags not stated. The Intel results directory is named benches/intel-msvc, suggesting a Windows MSVC toolchain.
hardware: 'Intel i9' (exact model not stated) and 'Apple M1'
tradeoffs: no_std and no unsafe, tiny crate (0.8 s clean build on an i9, per README). Rust crate only; no C API or C bindings found, so it is not callable from C++ without writing a wrapper. QOI itself compresses worse than PNG and is limited to 8-bit RGB/RGBA.
caveats: The only comparison is against another QOI implementation, so it says nothing about libpng or libjpeg-turbo. Encode gain is small (7 to 14 percent). In the repo's own benches/m1/rapid.md (the same run that produced the rapid_qoi row) the qoi column reads decode 1.161 ms vs rapid_qoi 1.100 ms (about 5 percent faster) and encode 1.614 ms vs 1.836 ms (rapid_qoi 14 percent slower), so the README's M1 row mixes numbers from benches/m1/reference.md and rapid.md. The README i9 rapid_qoi row (1.404 / 2.520 ms) also differs slightly from benches/intel-msvc/rapid.md (1.447 / 2.582 ms). The README labels the baseline as the 'Reference implementation' phoboslab/qoi, but the current bench source calls the qoi crate; the reference.md outputs may come from an older bench version. CPU model of the i9 and compiler flags are missing. A decoder correctness fix ('clamp QOI_OP_RUN split to remaining output length', 2026-06-29) landed after the README numbers were written.
found_via: Hacker News web search 'Show HN lossless image compression faster than PNG smaller and faster' surfaced the QOI threads ('QOI: Lossless Image Compression in O(n) Time', 'QOI'); thread pages cannot be opened here, so the QOI topic page github.com/topics/qoi led to this repo. README, benches reports and bench source read via github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com.

name: Gamut (QOI and QOIX codecs in the D image library)
baseline: PNG via stb (the README row 'PNG (stb)', presumably stb_image and stb_image_write); not libpng
workload: Decode and encode speed in Mpixels/s and bits per pixel on '8-bit color images' for PNG (stb), QOI and QOIX (Gamut's QOI derivative with better predictors plus an LZ4 stage); dataset and machine not stated.
claimed_speedup: README 'Why QOIX?' table (decode mpps / encode mpps / bits per pixel): PNG (stb) 89.73 / 14.34 / 10.29693; QOI 201.9 / 150.8 / 10.35162; QOIX 179.0 / 125.0 / 7.93607. QOIX vs PNG (stb): 2.0x faster decode, 8.7x faster encode, 23 percent fewer bits per pixel (all derived from page data). README text: 'QOIX and QOI generally outperforms PNG in decoding speed and encoding speed.'
tradeoffs: D library (DUB package), nothrow @nogc @safe and usable with -betterC; no C API or C bindings found, so not directly callable from C++. QOIX is a custom format whose bitstream 'may change between major Gamut tags', so it is not a storage format. QOIX is slower than QOI (179.0 vs 201.9 Mpps decode) in exchange for smaller files. Optional WebP and JPEG XL decoders add BSD-3-Clause code (configuration 'boost+mit+bsd3'); dub.json declares 'BSL-1.0+MIT'.
caveats: Table has no hardware, dataset, compiler or flags, and the repo has no benchmark folder (only a convert tool with a --time option), so it is not reproducible from the repo. The win comes from the QOI and QOIX formats, not from a faster PNG or JPEG codec; the baseline is stb's PNG path, not libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp or libavif. Low notability and a single self-measured table.
found_via: Hacker News web search 'Show HN lossless image compression faster than PNG smaller and faster' surfaced the QOI threads; thread pages cannot be opened here, so the QOI topic page github.com/topics/qoi led to this repo. README, LICENSE and dub.json read via github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com.
